1. Vide this judgment I shall dispose off the suit for eviction, recovery of arrears and mesne profit,
filed by the plaintiff against the defendant.

1 2. Brief facts as averrred in the plaint are that plaintiff is the legal and absolute owner of ground floor portion towards Street no. 28 of built-up property bearing no. 3269-3271/27-28, Beadon Pura,
Karol Bagh, New Delhi-110 005, admeasuring 250 Sq. ft. (hereinafter referred to as "plaintiff's property").
3. The plaintiff had let out a shop towards gali/street no. 28 (hereinafter referred to as "suit property" as shown in red in the site plan attached with the plaint) of his property (plaintiff's property) to the defendant since 01.04.2017 for running a food joint in the name and style of "Harihar Bhojnalya" on a monthly rent of Rs. 50,000/- (Fifty Thousand Rupees) excluding electricity, GST and Water charges. Document confirming the same was registered by way of Lease Deed/Rent Agreement dated 09.03.2020 for a period from 01.10.2019 to 31.03.2020.
4. It is further averred in the plaint that after expiry of the original tenancy period from 01.10.2019 to 31.03.2020, the tenancy period was renewed orally due to covid pandemic to help the defendant in such a pandemic situation. The defendant assured plaintiff that after pandemic got over and things normalized, he would clear outstanding arrears pertaining to the rent of the said property. 
Despite repeated requests by the plaintiff, the defendant failed to clear outstanding rent and did not pay a single penny to plaintiff towards arrears of rent, GST and water charges.
5. It is further averred in the plaint that defendant was aware that plaintiff had became Covid positive and taking undue advantage of health issues affecting plaintiff, after Covid, defendant failed to pay arrears of rent. All requests made by the plaintiff, who is a senior citizen, went in vain. In this manner arrears of rent to the tune of Rs.12,00,000/- excluding electricity, GST and water charges became due payable by the defendant to the plaintiff. The plaintiff informed the defendant that his tenancy period had got over, however, defendant failed to vacate the tenanted premises despite requests made by the plaintiff and also failed to clear arrears of rent and thus plaintiff was constrained to terminate the defendant's tenancy and got served legal notice dated 15.04.2022 upon him. The defendant instead of clearing the arrears of rent, started neglecting the tenanted premises to such an extent that it became extremely dilapidated and now it requires major/extensive repairs/reconstruction. In such circumstances, plaintiff is not desirous to continue with the tenancy of the defendant. 
6. It is also averred in the plaint that defendant has filed a false and fictitious suit for mandatory injunction bearing suit no. CS SCJ/2817/2021 against the plaintiff to avoid liability to pay arrears of rent and to postpone handing over of peaceful possession of the suit property to the plaintiff which is being contested by the plaintiff. Aggrieved by the acts of the defendant, plaintiff has filed the present suit praying:
(i) firstly, for decree of possession of the suit property. 
(ii) secondly, decree for recovery of arrears of rent @ Rs.50,000/- per month w.e.f.
April 2020 till the date defendant hands over physical possession of the suit property to plaintiff, and Jahawar Lal Vohra Through Poa Rajesh ... vs Rajiv Kumar on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10543617/
2 (iii) thirdly, decree of mesne profits since April 2020 till date of handing over of peaceful possession of the suit property by defendant to plaintiff. 
7. Defendant has contested the suit by filing the written statement. By way of preliminary objection,
it is alleged that plaintiff has filed the present suit to harass and humiliate the defendant. It is further alleged the plaintiff has unnecessarily dragged defendant in various litigations without any just, reasonable and genuine grounds. The plaintiff has also suppressed vital and material facts. 
Although it is claimed that suit is barred by the provisions of Order VI Rule 15 CPC and also U/o VII Rule 11(a, b, c, d) of CPC as well as Section 6 and 12 of Commercial Courts Act, the said pleas have not been substantiated by cogent averments. 
8. On merits, it is denied that plaintiff is legal and absolute owner of the plaintiff's property. It is alleged that plaintiff is the person of quarrelsome nature who regularly quarrels with the defendant. 
It is denied that the suit property was let out to defendant since 01.04.2017 for running a food joint in the name and style of "Harihar Bhojnayala" on monthly rent of Rs.50,000/- excluding electricity,
GST and water charges. It is claimed that the suit property is purely a residential property and no commercial activity is going on in it. The defendant is merely doing the work of food packing and that the suit property is not available for sitting of customers or any kind of commercial activity. It is further stated that defendant entered into an oral agreement with the plaintiff who claimed to be the owner of the suit property. Though defendant requested plaintiff several times to show the title documents of the said property to him, plaintiff did not do so on one pretext or the other. 
9. It is further averred in the written statement that when the defendant had taken the suit property on rent, he had requested plaintiff to convert the said residential property into a commercial property and execute a registered agreement for purpose of taking the NOC/certificate from police,
Fire department and MCD but plaintiff failed to do so. In absence of necessary NOCs/Certificates,
defendant is unable to run his business in the name and style of Harihar Bhojnalaya. It is further averred that in the month of August and September, 2019, defendant had spent a sum of Rs.13,50,000/- for renovation of the suit property, after taking oral permission of plaintiff, with assurance that the same would be deducted from rent and the period of lease would be extended for five years. The plaintiff intentionally and deliberately with malafide intention and ulterior motive got mentioned period of lease from 01.10.2019 to 31.03.2020 instead of 01.10.2019 to 01.09.2024 thereby cheating the defendant and playing fraud upon him. The plaintiff also assured defendant that money invested by him in the suit property would be adjusted @ Rs.25,000/- per month from the monthly rent. The suit property was let out for five years with provision of extension of lease period with the consent of the parties. The plaintiff further assured defendant that he would get the property converted to commercial from residential at his own expenses and defendant would not be liable to pay any expenditure for the same. The plaintiff was to cooperate with defendant in getting NOCs/license etc. for running Harihar Bhojnalaya. The plaintiff, however, failed to keep his word due to which defendant was unable to run business of bhojnalaya. The plaintiff caused wrongful loss to defendant by failing to give adjustment in the rent due and payable by defendant and rather demanded cash payment towards rent and in this manner he collected monthly rent of Rs.50,000/-
per month in cash from defendant.

3 10. It is further averred that in the month of November and December 2021, plaintiff pressurised defendant to increase rent from Rs.50,000/- to Rs.70,000/- p.m. and also tried to dispossess the defendant from the suit property due to which defendant was compelled to file civil suit bearing CS SCJ No.2817/2021 titled as 'Rajiv Kumar Vs. Jawahar Lal Vohra'. In the said suit, plaintiff filed written statement and admitted investment of Rs.13,50,000/- in the suit property by the defendant. 
On 03.12.2023, Sh.D.N. Chaturvedi, counsel for plaintiff made a statement that plaintiff would not dispossess the defendant from the suit property without the due process of law as he has already filed a suit for eviction and mesne profit. The suit filed by defendant was disposed off in terms of the undertaking given by the counsel for plaintiff. 
11. It is claimed that the plaintiff had been taking rent in cash continuously till the month of June,
2023 without issuing receipts despite repeated requests made by defendant. The defendant asserts that he has paid rent upto June 2023 and does not have any liability to pay the alleged rent. It also alleged that the plaintiff is also not ready to adjust sum of Rs.13,50,000/-, invested by defendant, for renovation of the suit property as promised by him. 
12. It is denied that plaintiff had renewed the tenancy orally after 31.03.2020 to help the defendant due to Covid or that he had permitted defendant to clear outstanding arrears pertaining to rent of the property later on. It is stated that plaintiff had collected rent amount in cash from defendant on the pretext that property was of residential nature and in case defendant paid rent through account transfer or cheque he would have difficulty in filing tax return as well as payment of tax to MCD. It is reiterated that defendant paid rent in cash upto June, 2023 to plaintiff. It is also stated that neither any rent nor GST, electricity and water charges are due and payable by defendant since plaintiff has liability for adjustment of a sum of Rs.13,50,000/- invested by defendant in renovation of the suit property. 
13. It is denied that a sum of Rs.12,00,000/- excluding electricity charges and water charges and GST amounting to Rs.90,000/- are due and payable by defendant to the plaintiff. It is further denied that defendant is liable to pay damages for use and occupation of the premises @
Rs.70,000/- p.m. w.e.f. April, 2020. It is stated that tenancy of defendant was to expire in the year 2024 and that there is no question of termination of license/tenancy of defendant as claimed by plaintiff. The defendant reiterates that plaintiff has filed present suit to harass him and has accordingly prayed that the suit filed by plaintiff be dismissed. 
14. The plaintiff has filed replication reiterating averments made in the plaint and denying contra averments made in the written statement. It is stated that defendant has admitted ownership of plaintiff in suit for permanent injunction bearing no.CS SCJ/2817/2021 filed by him and cannot be permitted to change his stand to cause wrongful loss to the plaintiff. It is admitted that the tenancy of defendant commenced w.e.f. 01.04.2017 for running food joint in the name and style of Harihar bhojnalaya. It is denied that defendant is doing work of food packing only from the suit premises or that the same is only a residential property. 
15. Relying upon the electricity bill of the suit property it is stated that plaintiff is being charged in category of "Non- domestic" i.e. commercial category. The property tax is also paid by plaintiff for Jahawar Lal Vohra Through Poa Rajesh ... vs Rajiv Kumar on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10543617/
4 commercial property and this fact is further confirmed by Sale Deed registered in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff has reproduced the "Schedule of property" in para 1 of the reply on merits. 
16. It is further averred that in para 6 of the plaint in suit for permanent injunction bearing CS SCJ/2817/2021 also defendant has averred that he has obtained permission from Delhi Police,
MCD, Delhi Pollution Control Committee to run Bhojnalaya and further obtained license from Department of Food Safety to run the same and has registered his restaurant "Harihar Bhojnalaya"
with GST. In view of the same, he is not permitted to take stand that suit property is of residential nature. 
17. As regards defendant's plea that he had spent a sum of Rs.13,50000/- for renovation of the suit property, it is prayed that defendant be put to strict proof thereof. It is reiterated that defendant is liable to pay all the outstanding rent, water and electricity charges, GST and mesne profit till such time that he hands over vacant and peaceful possession of the suit property to the plaintiff. It is denied that plaintiff agreed for renovation of the suit property by the defendant or that he had invested a sum of Rs.13,50,000/- for the same. Rest of the contra averments made in the written statement have also been controverted on merits. 
18. From the pleadings of parties, following issues were framed:-
1) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to decree for recovery of possession of the shop at the ground floor portion towards street No.28 of built up property bearing No.3269 to 3271/27-28, Beadonpura, Karol Bagh, Delhi-5, against defendant? OPP 2) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to recover arrears of rent at the rate of Rs.50,000/- per month w.e.f.
April, 2020 till the vacant peaceful possession of suit property i.e. shop at the ground floor portion towards street No.28 of built up property bearing No.3269 to 3271/27-28, Beadonpura, Karol Bagh,
Delhi-5, is handed over to him by the defendant? OPP 3) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to recovery mesne profits w.e.f. April, 2020 from defendant, if so,
at what rate and which period?OPP 4) Relief.
19. In order to prove its case, plaintiff has examined Sh. Rajesh Vohra, his attorney, as PW1. He has reiterated the facts averred in the plaint in his affidavit Ex.PW-1/A and relied upon following documents:-
 S.No. Details of documents Exhibit  1. Site plan of suit property Ex.PW1/1  2. Original POA in his favour Ex.PW1/1A  3. 5  4. Photocopy of legal notice dated 15.04.2022 Ex.PW1/4 20. During his cross-examination, PW1 deposed that the suit premises were let out to defendant by his father in the year 2017 at monthly rent of Rs.50,000/- per month. The defendant used to deposit rent in the bank account of his father and had deposited rent upto 31.03.2020. He had not filed statement of account of his father on Court record. His father had not executed any other Power of Attorney in his favour except Ex.PW-1/1A which is on Court record. 
21. During his further cross-examination , he (PW1) termed it correct that the verification clause of the plaint did not mention specific date and that on the plaint word 'deponent' was mentioned instead of 'plaintiff' and that there was no date under the signatures of plaintiff under the word 'deponent'. He further termed it correct that valuation of the suit property had not been given in the plaint. He then deposed that the lease deed Ex.PW- 1/2 was got prepared by defendant. He termed it correct that on lease deed Ex.PW-1/2, on first page, against the column 'description of documents',
it was mentioned 'article 35 (ii) lease with security upto 5 years'. He termed it incorrect that the stamp paper for the lease deed was purchased by his father or that the same was also got prepared by his father. He termed it correct that in the column 'stamp duty paid by' name of his father Sh.
Jawahar Lal Vohra was mentioned and that his name was also mentioned against the column 'purchased by'.
22. During his further cross-examination , PW1 was put printed matter on the backside of lease deed Ex.PW-1/2. He termed it correct that thereupon against column 'deed name' it was mentioned 'lease and lease with security upto 5 years'. He expressed his inability to state the stamp duty payable for registration of the lease deed or if it was 2% of yearly rent. The PW1 denied that lease deed was got prepared by him and his father or that they had got written period of lease deed as 6 months instead of 5 years fraudulently in the recitals of the lease deed. 
23 . During his further cross-examination , PW1 deposed that the suit property was got renovated before it was let out to the defendant but was unable to state the exact month, year or date of said renovation. He further deposed that his father was paying commercial tax in respect of the suit property and had paid the same upto date. The PW1 denied that the suit property was never got renovated by his father. He further denied that besides the rent transferred into the bank account of his father, he used to take some part of rent in cash also. His father was an income tax assessee and reflected his rental income in his returns. 
24. The PW1 further deposed that prior to lease deed Ex.PW-1/2 also a lease deed/ rent agreement was executed between his father and the defendant and that the same was in possession of defendant. He denied that all the lease deeds were in possession of his father or that there was no lease deed executed prior to Ex.PW-1/2 or that for this reason copy thereof had not been filed along with the present suit. The PW1 denied that the defendant had paid rent upto June, 2023 or that he used to pay rent in cash and through bank transfer from 01.04.2017 upto June, 2023. He further denied that the rent of the suit premises was increased to Rs.70,000/- illegally from June, 2022 or that the defendant continued to pay rent @ Rs.50,000/- per month up till June, 2023 or that Jahawar Lal Vohra Through Poa Rajesh ... vs Rajiv Kumar on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10543617/
6 thereafter he stopped paying rent to his father since he was insisting on rent @ Rs.70,000/- per month. 
25. The PW1 further denied that defendant had requested his father to issue NOC and to deposit conversion charges so that he could obtain licence from Delhi Police and MCD for running his business of food packing and eatery from the suit premises or that since the defendant failed to obtain licence, his business remained closed for 4 months or that defendant suffered losses of lacs of rupees due to the same. The PW1 further denied that MCD had demanded conversion charges of Rs.47 Lacs which plaintiff failed to deposit due to which Delhi Police did not issue licence to the defendant. 
26. The PW1 termed it correct that the defendant had filed a suit for injunction against his father. 
He, however, denied that the defendant had to file the said suit as his father was trying to dispossess the defendant forcibly from the suit property. The PW1 termed it correct that in the said suit their counsel had given a statement that since a suit for eviction had already been filed, his father would not dispossess the defendant without the due process of law. The PW1 denied that defendant had carried out renovations in the suit property in August / September, 2019 or that he had spent a sum of Rs.13,50,000/- which was to be adjusted partly towards the rent for repayment by his father or that the renovation work went on for about 2 months in his supervision. The PW1 termed it correct that his father had filed written statement, Ex.PW1/D1, in CS SCJ/2817/2021.
27. The PW1 denied that legal notice Ex.PW-1/4 was never sent by him on behalf of his father to the defendant or that he had no right to send the said legal notice. The PW1 expressed his inability to state if the defendant is carrying on his business on the basis of licence issued by FSSAI or if he had been unable to procure licence from MCD till date. The PW1 denied that defendant was liable to pay rent to his father @ Rs.50,000/- per month from July, 2023 onwards only or that the legal notice Ex.PW-1/4 was premature as the lease of defendant was for 5 years. He further denied that he did not have Power of Attorney from his father when notice Ex.PW-1/4 was sent by him on behalf of his father to the defendant. The PW1 also denied that he had filed the present suit as he and his father wanted to pressurize defendant to pay rent @ Rs.70,000/- per month or that the defendant had stopped paying rent from July, 2023 as his father refused to adjust sum of Rs.13,50,000/-, spent by defendant in renovation of the suit premises, either partly or fully. The PW1 denied that defendant did not have liability to pay any sum of money to his father as he had already invested a sum of Rs.13,50,000/- in the suit premises which was yet to be adjusted.

30. During his cross-examination, the DW1 deposed that Lease Deed Ex.PW1/2 had his photograph at Point encircled 'X' and his signatures at Point 'X1' on all four pages. He termed it correct that the lease deed Ex.PW1/2 was got registered on 09.03.2020 at the office of Sub-Registrar, Asaf Ali Road. 
31. The DW1 further deposed that he had filed a suit for permanent injunction against the plaintiff and that the copy of plaint was Ex.PW1/D1. He termed it correct that in para 2 of Ex.PW1/D1 he had stated that the defendant therein (plaintiff in the present suit) is the owner of the ground floor portion towards Street No.28, of built up property bearing no.3269 to 3271/27-28, Beadonpura,
Karol Bagh, New Delhi-110005. He further deposed that he used to make payment of rent of Rs.50,000/- to plaintiff by cheque and did so from the year 2017 to March, 2020 and that thereafter, he started paying rent @ Rs.50,000/- per month in cash to the plaintiff and had paid rent in cash to plaintiff from April, 2020 to July, 2023.
32. At this stage, in response to specific question as to whether he had paid rent @ Rs.59,000/- per month to plaintiff from 04.09.2019 to 29.02.2020 by way of cheque drawn on HDFC Bank, the DW1 answered in affirmative. He volunteered to state that Rs.50,000/- was towards rent while Rs.9,000/- was GST payable thereupon. 
33. When asked whether he had taken FSSAI license on 23.12.2019, the DW1 deposed that the had taken the same in the year 2020 but was unable to remember the actual date of it. 
When confronted with Ex.DW1/P1 i.e. photocopy of registration license no.23319001002691 which formed part of Ex.PW1/D1, the DW1 admitted that it was photocopy of FSSAI license which he had filed alongwith the plaint in suit no. 2817/2021 titled as 'Rajiv Kumar Vs. Jawahar Lal Vohra'. He termed it correct that date of issue of license was mentioned as 23.12.2019.

During his further cross-examination , DW1 deposed that he was earlier residing at a tenanted premises at 4530-A/11, Jai Mata Market, Tri Nagar, Onkar Nagar, Delhi-110035 and was residing at 2470/193, Ganeshpura B, Tri Nagar, Delhi-110035 since last about 3 years. 47. I have heard the learned Counsels for the parties and have also perused the record as well as written submissions filed on behalf of parties and my findings on aforesaid issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 Whether the plaintiff is entitled to decree for recovery of possession of the shop at the ground floor portion towards street No.28 of built up property bearing No.3269 to 3271/27- 28, Beadonpura, Karol Bagh, Delhi-5, against defendant? OPP 48. Onus of proving this issue was on plaintiff. The plaintiff who is the owner and landlord of the suit property seeks to recover its possession from the defendant to whom he had let out the property since 01.04.2017 for running a food joint in the name and style of "Harihar Bhojnalya" on a monthly rent of Rs. 50,000/- (Fifty Thousand Rupees) excluding electricity, GST and Water charges. 
Subsequently, a registered Lease Deed/Rent Agreement dated 09.03.2020 was also executed between the parties for a period from 01.10.2019 to 31.03.2020. The plaintiff claims that thereafter he renewed the tenancy orally due to Covid pandemic to help the defendant tide over the pandemic situation, however the defendant stopped paying rent of the suit property w.e.f. April 2020. He also failed to hand over its vacant and peaceful possession to plaintiff despite termination of tenancy by the plaintiff vide legal notice dated 15.04.2022. The plaintiff has examined his son/attorney as PW1 to prove his case. 
49. The defendant, on the other hand, has challenged the ownership of the plaintiff as also the nature of suit property by claiming that it was let out for residential purpose. He has alleged that despite repeated requests plaintiff failed to convert the suit property which was a residential property into commercial property and to execute registered agreement to enable him to take NOC/certificate from police, Fire department and MCD due to which defendant was unable to run his business in the name and style of Harihar Bhojnalaya. He is merely doing work of food packing from the suit property as there is no place available for sitting of customers or any kind of commercial activity. The defendant also claims to have spent a sum of Rs.13,50,000/- on the renovation of the suit property, with the oral permission of plaintiff and with further understanding that the said amount would be adjusted @ Rs.25,000/- per month from the monthly rent and that the lease of the suit property would be extended for five years.

Though registration of lease agreement/rent agreement is admitted, it is alleged that plaintiff intentionally and deliberately mentioned period of lease from 01.10.2019 to 30.03.2020 instead of 01.10.2019 to 01.09.2024. ISSUE NO.2 Whether the plaintiff is entitled to recover arrears of rent at the rate of Rs.50,000/- per month w.e.f. April, 2020 till the vacant peaceful possession of suit property i.e. shop at the ground floor portion towards street No.28 of built up property bearing No.3269 to 3271/27-28,
Beadonpura, Karol Bagh, Delhi-5, is handed over to him by the defendant?
According to plaintiff, the defendant was to pay monthly rent of Rs.50,000/- excluding electrity, GST and water charges for the suit premises.
In these circumstances, the mesne profit is to be calculated on basis of rate of rent payable by defendant to the plaintiff i.e. @ Rs.50,000 per month excluding GST, electricity and water charges.
The electricity and water charges would be payable on basis of actual consumption by the defendant.
Since the rate of rent agreed upon between the parties was Rs.50,000/- per month as per lease deed/rent agreement Ex.PW1/2, the plaintiff is entitled to enhance the rate of rent by 10%
w.e.f. 01.10.2022 by which date the tenancy of defendant had already been terminated by the plaintiff.
Hence, the defendant shall be liable to pay mesne profit @ Rs.50,000 per month excluding GST, electricity and water charges from 16.05.2022 till 01.10.2022 and thereafter @ Rs.55,000/- per month i.e. prevailing rent of Rs.50,000/- plus 10% increase in rent, exclusing GST, electricity and water charges till such time he hands over vacant and peaceful possession of the suit premises to the plaintiff.
The rate of damages payable by defendant would be liable to increase by further 10% after three years from 01.10.2022 i.e. from 01.10.2025 in case he fails to vacate the suit premises by then and the rate of damages shall continue to increase @ 10% after every three years thereafter in the event he fails to vacate the suit premises and to hand over its possession to plaintiff.

71.

, is passed in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant.

The plaintiff shall convey water and electricity charges payable by defendant from April, 2020 till 15.05.2022 on basis of actual consumption and in the event the same is not available the mean value of water and electricity charges paid by defendant for three months/cycles prior to April, 2020.
The same be conveyed by plaintiff to defendant within two weeks of passing of the judgment and decree in the present case.

(iii) A decree for mesne profit @ Rs.50,000 per month excluding GST, electricity and water charges,
is passed in favour of plaintiff and against defendant, from 16.05.2022 till 01.10.2022 and thereafter @ Rs.55,000/- per month i.e. Rs.50,000/- plus 10% increase in rent, exclusing GST, electricity and water charges till such time defendant hands over vacant and peaceful possession of the suit premises to the plaintiff.
The rate of damages payable by defendant would be liable to increase by further 10% after three years from 01.10.2022 i.e. from 01.10.2025 in case he fails to vacate the suit premises by then and the rate of damages shall continue to increase @ 10% after every three years thereafter.
